title: Automatic backups
intro: Every day the app saves a zip like "Export a backup…" (notes, attachments, state and trash; no keys or passwords).
enableHint: If the computer is off or asleep at that time, the app catches up when you start it again.
folderHintNoDefault: Leave empty to use the Backups folder next to the vault.
openFolderFailed: The folder could not be opened. Check the drive or choose another folder, then try again.
timeHint: Time of day on the 24-hour clock, for example 21:00.
timeInvalid: Enter a time on the 24-hour clock, for example 21:00.
keepHint: From {{min}} to {{max}}. The app only deletes old backups it made itself; other files in the folder are always kept.

status.retry: The app will try again at {{when}}.

failure.folder-missing: the backup folder was not found. Plug the drive back in or choose another folder.
failure.not-a-folder: the backup path is a file, not a folder.
failure.not-writable: the app cannot write to the backup folder. Choose another folder.
failure.disk-full: the drive is full. Free some space or choose another drive.
failure.inside-vault: the backup folder is inside the vault, so each backup would copy itself. Choose a folder outside the vault.
failure.inside-app: the backup folder is inside the app's own folder. Choose another folder.
failure.too-large: the vault is larger than one zip file can hold.
failure.busy: another backup is running. Wait a moment and try again.
failure.failed: something unexpected went wrong. Try again in a few minutes.

folderProblem.inside-vault: This folder is inside the vault, so it cannot be used. Choose a folder outside the vault.
folderProblem.inside-app: This folder is inside the app's own folder, so it cannot be used. Choose another folder.
folderProblem.not-absolute: Enter a full path, for example D:\Backups.

github.title: Push to GitHub
github.intro: Optional: push the vault's version history to a private GitHub repository after each automatic backup.
github.enable: Push to GitHub after each automatic backup
github.missing: Fill in the repository address and access token first to turn this on.
github.noGit: Pushing to GitHub needs Git. Install Git for Windows to turn it on.
github.noHistory: Version history is off for this vault, so nothing can be pushed yet.
github.remoteHint: Use a private repository. The address starts with https://.
github.tokenHint: Create a fine-grained token for this repository only, with Contents: Read and write.

failure.auth: GitHub did not accept the access token. Check the token and its access to this repository.
failure.network: GitHub could not be reached. Check the connection and try again.
failure.rejected: GitHub refused because the repository already has other changes. Use an empty repository or another branch.
failure.no-git: Git is not installed. Install Git for Windows.
failure.no-history: version history is off for this vault.
failure.not-configured: fill in the repository address and access token first.
failure.failed: something unexpected went wrong. Try again in a few minutes.
failure.interrupted: the app closed while pushing. Press Push now to push again.

secret.empty: Paste the key into the field before saving.

saveErrors.not-absolute: Enter a full path, for example D:\Backups.
saveErrors.invalid-path: The path contains characters that cannot be used.
saveErrors.https-only: The address must start with https://.
saveErrors.credentials-in-url: Do not put a user name or token in the address. Paste the token into the access token field.
saveErrors.branch-format: A branch name may only contain letters, digits, dots, dashes, underscores and /.
saveErrors.token-format: This token does not look right. Paste the whole GitHub token again.
saveErrors.out-of-range: The value is outside the allowed range.
saveErrors.pattern: This value does not have the right form.
